# Accessibility statement

This statement covers OxRSE Training, the teaching website of the [Oxford Research Software Engineering group](https://www.rse.ox.ac.uk/) at the University of Oxford.
This site hosts a deployment of the open-source teaching platform [Gutenberg](https://github.com/OxfordRSE/gutenberg), which is maintained by the OxRSE team.

We want as many people as possible to be able to use it.
For example, you should be able to:

- skip straight to the main content with the "Skip to main content" link
- choose a light or dark theme, with a default for your system setting
- zoom in without losing content, and use the site on a narrow phone screen
- hear mathematical notation read out by a screen reader

## Known limitations

- Much of the course material is collated from other sources. Some images and diagrams in it do not have text alternatives, and some videos it links to may not have captions.
- We have tested parts of the site with screen readers, but not it's entirity. In particular, courses and their associated content.
- The site is only available in English.
- The material diagram pages are not keyboard accessible, and the diagrams themselves are not accessible to screen readers. But the same relationship between courses and material is available in the course pages, which are accessible.

## Reporting a problem

If anything on the site is hard to use, or you cannot use it at all, please [report it on GitHub](https://github.com/OxfordRSE/gutenberg/issues/new?template=accessibility.yml).
It helps to give as much detail as possible about what you were trying to do, including which device, browser and any assistive technology you used.

Reporting needs a free GitHub account.
If you do not have one, you can contact us by [email](mailto:alasdair.wilson@dtc.ox.ac.uk).
We read every report, but we cannot promise how soon we can implement the necessary changes.

## Technical information

We aim to meet the [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), version 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) at level AA.
The site has not been audited independently, so we cannot say for certain that it does; the limitations we know of are listed above.

## How we tested the site

The site is tested with both axe-core and lighthouse,free accessibility testing tools, and the integrated screen reader and keyboard navigation in the Firefox browser.

This statement was prepared on 11 November 2026.
